key_insight: A phononic subsurface embedded in a flat plate can either amplify or suppress sustained vortex-shedding oscillations, with its placement along the chord strongly determining whether the coupled flow-structure system benefits or destabilizes the unsteady forces.
engineering_relevance: Properly positioned phononic subsurfaces could passively reduce vibration and aerodynamic load fluctuations in separated-flow applications without materially changing mean lift or drag.
method: High-fidelity immersed boundary simulations of fully separated flow over a flat plate with an embedded phononic subsurface.
The subsurface is modeled as a grounded diatomic chain coupled to a compliant plate segment.
Two controls are studied: chordwise position and resonant displacement growth rate (behavioral amplitude envelope).
evidence_signal: The simulations identify four position-dependent limit-cycle regimes, including a configuration that cuts lift oscillation amplitude by over 30% and drag oscillation amplitude by over 50% while changing mean lift and drag by less than 0.5%.
watch_item: Performance is highly position-sensitive and depends on transient resonant behavior, so practical designs will need careful tuning to avoid regimes that amplify unsteady loads.
paper_title: Interaction of Sustained Vortex Shedding with a Phononic Subsurface: Effect of Positioning and Resonant Characteristics
